home.aboutSummary: Architecture graduate of Drexel's 2+4 program, now managing adaptive reuse projects in Philadelphia. Strongest on constraint-heavy problems and the early design work that resolves them.

paragraphs: Architecture graduate of the 2+4 program at Drexel University, currently managing adaptive reuse and state-of-good-repair projects in Philadelphia.

My strengths are in early design and conceptual development: diagramming, rendering, and communicating intent. I am comfortable translating complex ideas into clear narratives for clients and consultants, and I work best on constraint-heavy problems.
I am looking for a civically minded role that prioritizes sustainability and community while broadening my technical range, with the aim of contributing to Philadelphia's built environment.

routes.label: Professional work
routes.blurb: Naugatuck is a mixed-use building for Pennrose, drawn at WRT Planning + Design and now in construction. Pride in Place is the planning work, a district resolved from the street module upward. Block Core and Kensington Core follow one scheme from a single corner to a full block. A résumé and references are on the About page.

routes.label: Design and research
routes.blurb: Post Scarcity is the thesis, awarded the 2025 Pearson Prize Silver Medal, and is laid out as a walkthrough from premise to building. Pride in Place carries the supporting analysis: circulation studies, street modules, and the mapping the plan answers to.

routes.label: A quick overview
routes.blurb: Kensington Core includes four short films. Garden Schools sets three schools within a single shared landscape. Every project opens with its images, and the timeline below runs from the most recent backward.
